topics: success criteria; workload sizing; benchmark plan; model shortlist; multilingual & finance-domain needs; timelines & next steps
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 15:00 PT, Duration ~52m, Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Rivera (Cobalt Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Cobalt Staff ML Eng), Priya Singh (Product)

[00:00] Jamie Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Maya Rivera: yeah loud and clear, thanks Jamie. we got the calendar invite, super excited to scope this out.
[00:12] Jamie Chen: great. quick round robin — i'm Jamie, AE on the account; Samir here is our SE and will lead the benchmark/tuning side. can you do quick intros?
[00:22] Maya Rivera: maya—i run ml for cobalt. focus is internal insights and multi-lingual summarization for finance docs.
[00:28] Ethan Cole: ethan, i own infra and evaluation pipelines. we'll provide sample logs and do the pilot infra.
[00:32] Priya Singh: priya, product. timeline is Q2 production goal, but open to a phased approach.

[00:40] Jamie Chen: perfect. high level agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, which open models to test, benchmarks and timelines. does that align?
[00:46] Priya Singh: yes, sounds good.

[00:50] Samir Patel: i want to flag upfront — from experience, we usually recommend starting with 7B/13B quantized open models for cost/latency, and then test a 70B variant for quality headroom. but we need to understand your quality bar and latency SLOs.

[01:06] Maya Rivera: our success criteria are twofold: 1) semantic accuracy on financial Q&A and summarization (ROUGE + human score threshold), and 2) latency under 800ms p50 for single-turn user queries. cost target is around $0.005 per query ideally, but flexible if accuracy jumps.

[01:28] Ethan Cole: also data residency — any logs stay in our VPC during the private pilot. security's a blocker for us later, but for POC we can use redwood dedicated or private depending on options.

[01:42] Jamie Chen: noted — we can run the pilot on Redwood Dedicated or Private. for the initial bench we usually run in Hosted with isolated customer workspace, but we'll follow your residency needs. Samir, can you walk through the workload sizing we need?

[01:53] Samir Patel: sure. to scope we need: avg tokens per request, peak qps, concurrency, and distribution of languages. for a 1k baseline run we ask for a representative sample. e.g., if avg tokens is 150 and peak qps is 20, that informs model selection and batching config.

[02:12] Ethan Cole: we can export a week's worth — currently avg tokens ~220 for our long summarization tasks, but for quick Q&A it's 45 tokens. traffic is spiky, peak ~25 qps during market hours. language mix is 60% EN, 25% ES, 15% FR.

[02:31] Maya Rivera: domain is finance — lots of tickers, ledger phrases, and tables. we care about model handling of numeric reasoning and table-to-text. 

[02:44] Samir Patel: okay numeric reasoning + tables is tougher for smaller models. for open-model shortlist i'd propose we test: Mistral-Instruct-7B quantized, Llama 2-13B-chat quantized, Falcon-40B-instruct (8-bit), and a 70B family like Mistral-70B or Llama 3-70B if you want headroom. that's the starting shortlist.

[03:07] Maya Rivera: curious about multilingual — do these models support ES/FR out of box or do we need fine-tuning?

[03:13] Samir Patel: Mistral and Llama 2 have reasonable multilingual performance, but for finance-specific Spanish/French you may need a small domain-adaptive fine-tune or instruction tuning; alternatively a retrieval-augmented approach with domain docs helps a lot while keeping models smaller.

[03:29] Ethan Cole: for latency target (800ms p50) — what's realistic per model?

[03:34] Samir Patel: approximate p50 on a single A100-like GPU with quantization: 7B ~ 80-150ms, 13B ~ 150-350ms, 40B ~ 400-900ms depending on sequence length and KV cache; 70B is often >900ms without sharding/optimizations. but our runtime supports continuous batching and caching to help. these are rough numbers.

[03:56] Priya Singh: cost tradeoffs — can you ballpark cost per query for our avg token sizes?

[04:01] Samir Patel: rough rule of thumb: 7B quantized can be 3-8x cheaper than 70B per token. if your avg tokens per long summarization is 220, a 13B quantized run might be in the $0.003-0.01 per call range depending on batching and cache; 70B could be $0.02-0.08. we should run a benchmark to get precise numbers.

[04:22] Maya Rivera: ok makes sense. quality bar — we need to define evaluation. Ethan can you confirm your eval metrics?

[04:28] Ethan Cole: we'll do automatic metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/Exact match where appropriate) plus a small human eval (5-10 raters) for the top two models. also we'll include numeric accuracy checks for common table queries.

[04:39] Jamie Chen: great. proposed benchmark plan: customer provides 1k representative queries + expected outputs or eval rubric; Redwood runs models: Mistral-7B, Llama2-13B-chat, Falcon-40B, and a 70B if you want. We'll measure latency distribution, cost estimate, and quality. Run local human eval for top 2 models. Does that work?

[04:58] Maya Rivera: yes — include multilingual splits in the 1k so we see per-lang performance.

[05:05] Samir Patel: also capture sequence length buckets and table vs plain text so we can recommend quantization and batching settings. we'll add KV/prefix caching tests for repeated context scenarios.

[05:17] Priya Singh: timeline question — we want results to inform a Q2 decision. what's realistic?

[05:22] Jamie Chen: if you share logs by 2026-03-09 and we run the baseline week of 3/16, we can have preliminary results by 3/20-3/24. then a 2-week deep evaluation and human scoring would land in early April. does that map to Q2 gating?

[05:36] Maya Rivera: yes that fits.

[05:39] Ethan Cole: security — we will need SOC2 and data residency docs before production. for POC, we just need a data processing agreement and to confirm logs won't be retained beyond the test window.

[05:50] Jamie Chen: we'll share our security packet and we can sign an NDA/DP agreement. note: for on-prem or private deployments, we can arrange a private control plane and KMS integration — we discussed this previously.

[05:59] Samir Patel: technical note — if you plan to run on-prem or in your VPC, model quantization artifacts and kernel selection matter. we can provide recommended quantization recipes (int8/int4) and kernel configs for your GPU fleet.

[06:12] Maya Rivera: excellent. any blockers we're missing?

[06:15] Priya Singh: procurement review for dedicated capacity might take 3–4 weeks; we'll keep that parallel.

[06:21] Jamie Chen: recap then next steps: 1) Jamie sends benchmark template + open-model shortlist + pricing (3/6). 2) Ethan exports anonymized 1 week of request logs and 1k representative queries with language labels (3/9). 3) Samir runs baseline and shares preliminary results (week of 3/16). 4) schedule follow-up to review results (Jamie/Ethan to align calendar).

[06:42] Ethan Cole: i'll get the logs scrubbed and drop into the secure S3 link. one question — do you have a shared template for expected outputs? saves us time.

[06:48] Samir Patel: yes we'll include a small csv schema and rubric; also a link to a benchmark spreadsheet and instructions — i'll attach that in the follow-up email.

[06:56] Maya Rivera: quick follow: for multilingual, if the top model fails ES/FR, what's the recommended approach — fine-tune vs retrieval?

[07:02] Samir Patel: retrieval + few-shot prompting is often the fastest path; if long-term volume justifies it, a small domain-adaptive fine-tune (1-5% of dataset) can close the gap. we'll report per-lang deltas in the baseline.

[07:12] Priya Singh: perfect. sounds good. thanks team.

[07:16] Jamie Chen: thanks everyone, i'll send notes and artifacts after. we'll aim for the 3/16 baseline window. bye.

[07:22] (call ends)
questions: Which open models should we include in the initial benchmark?
What's the expected latency and cost tradeoff per model family?
Do we need domain-adaptive fine-tuning for ES/FR finance docs or is retrieval sufficient?
